name: Agents of Destruction
summary: At the outpost of Forest Song, Sentinel Luciel Starwhisper directs Alliance champions to strike deep into the Warsong Lumber Camp. The objective is to eliminate Overseer Gorthak, disable goblin-built shredders, and scatter the Horde deforesters ravaging eastern Ashenvale's ancient woodlands.

sections.title: A Scar in the Canopy
sections.body: The Warsong Lumber Camp represents an open wound across eastern Ashenvale. For the night elves, who hold the primeval trees sacred, the persistent clear-cutting is more than an economic territorial dispute—it is active desecration. Every strike against the lumber operations has only resulted in the Horde redoubling its logging, pushing further into ancient canopies.

sections.title: Reckless Destruction
sections.body: What enrages Sentinel Luciel Starwhisper most is not merely the logging, but its wanton carelessness. Overseer Gorthak's crew cuts far more timber than their wagons can haul away, leaving felled trunks to rot on the forest floor while metal blades and steam-powered shredders gnaw into fresh groves. Striking down Gorthak and destroying his machinery aims to shatter the camp's leadership before the woodland is hollowed out entirely.

faq.q: Why is the Horde cutting so much lumber in Ashenvale?
faq.answer: The orcish capital of Orgrimmar and the settlement of Durotar sit in arid, barren badlands devoid of large timber. The Warsong Outriders harvest Ashenvale's dense forest to fuel Horde construction and siegecraft, though Overseer Gorthak's operation cuts far beyond necessity, leaving piles of felled wood to simply rot.

Overseer Gorthak commands the Warsong Lumber Camp in eastern Ashenvale. Rather than slowing down under night elf pressure, Gorthak pushed his peons, scouts, and deforesters to increase their felling pace, earning the direct wrath of Sentinel Luciel Starwhisper.

faq.q: Where is this mission launched from?
aliases: where to start agents of destruction
faq.answer: The strike is ordered by Sentinel Luciel Starwhisper at Forest Song, a night elf outpost located in the eastern reaches of Ashenvale, just north of the border road and the Warsong logging grounds.

faq.q: Why are shredders operating in the woods?
faq.answer: The Horde employs goblin-engineered shredders—bipedal steam-driven contraptions armed with buzz saws—to accelerate logging. To the night elves, these smoking, oil-dripping machines are unnatural horrors that churn pristine glades into muddy wastelands.

faq.q: What happens to the lumber camp after Gorthak falls?
faq.answer: Killing Gorthak stuns the operation and halts the immediate waste, but Starwhisper acknowledges that the Horde will likely attempt to replace him. She vows to strike down any foreman or overseer who attempts to resume logging until the camp is entirely reclaimed by nature.

faq.q: Does the Alliance claim the cut wood?
faq.answer: No. The night elves view the slaughtered trees as a tragedy rather than a resource to be hoarded. Their aim is solely to halt the slaughter of living boughs and allow the forest time to heal.

angles.text: For the kaldorei, watching ancient trees cut down and abandoned to rot is an unendurable sacrilege. Reclaiming the eastern groves is a duty to Elune and the spirits of the woods.
The mechanical whine of goblin shredders tearing through Ashenvale's living timber pains any druid who communes with the wild, making Gorthak's camp an urgent target for cleansing.
The Warsong Shredders represent the crude, noisy peak of Venture Company-style goblin mechanical power adapted for military-scale land clearing.
Striking the Warsong Lumber Camp deprives the Horde of vital timber shipments while reinforcing the Alliance's contested hold on the Ashenvale borderlands.
